title: The First Millimeter Detection of a Non-Accreting Ultracool Dwarf
question: Is the ultracool dwarf TVLM 513-46546 detectable at millimeter wavelengths with ALMA, and what emission mechanism and spectrum does this imply?

what.value: Astrometric parameters (parallax/distance, proper motion) used for expected position

evidence.quote: Using the astrometric parameters reported by (cite: fbr13)

what.value: Combined radio/optical ephemeris predicting optical maximum BMJD 57150.028 and rotation period

evidence.quote: The combined radio/optical ephemeris described in that work predicts an optical maximum at $\text{BMJD} = 57150.028$

what.value: Published cm-band flux densities used in the broadband spectrum

evidence.quote: fit to our ALMA data and the measurements of (cite: ohbr06)

recipe.goal: Image ALMA data and measure source flux
recipe.method: Re-imaged calibrated visibilities; fitted a source model to the image

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA spectral index from sidebands
recipe.method: Imaged LSB and USB separately and derived spectral index

recipe.goal: Extract and test ALMA light curve for variability
recipe.method: Visibility-based light curves with other source subtracted; likelihood ratio test of constant vs exponentially fading flare, plus Bayes factor

recipe.goal: Calibrate and measure archival VLA fluxes
recipe.method: CASA calibration, aoflagger RFI flagging, point-source fits to images in three bands

recipe.goal: Time optical maximum from LT photometry
recipe.method: Aperture photometry with comparison stars; sinusoid fit with period fixed to literature
key_parameters: Apertures 1.6 times seeing; two brightest of four comparison stars used

recipe.goal: Assess emission mechanism and broadband spectrum
recipe.method: Rule out thermal, free-free (X-ray based estimate) and ECMI (cyclotron frequency field requirement); compare gyrosynchrotron model with data
assumptions: Free-free scaling S = 1e6 Jy * f_X for active low-mass stars

evidence.quote: we measure a flux density of $56 \pm 12$
a source that is 6.2$\sigma$ above the background noise
the flux density of the source is $66 \pm 8$
in about 7% of simulated realizations of the constant model

ALMA flux calibrator and flux-scale uncertainty

score_reason: Public data and simple measurements, but imaging, fitting and flare-test settings are unspecified.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a single point-source flux measurement with numeric results; recipe is simple though some settings are missing.
